data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘nāt’, meaning ‘night’. In Hindu mythology, Nanu is an epithet for the goddess Kali, who personifies the power of the universe and protects her devotees. The name Nanu carries the meaning “Night” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Nanu usually hope their child will grow to embody night and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the name Nanu is used as a term of endearment and is commonly used to address children or young girls fondly. It also exists as an alternative name for the goddess Kali, who is acclaimed for her fierce and protective presence.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Nanu, as a name for the goddess Kali, represents the primeval force that gives life, preserves, destroys, and reconstructs it. She is known to bestow her devotees with strength, courage, and protection. The name also connects to the idea of the eternal cycle of life and death as depicted by the night and day sequence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nanu in Sanskrit means "Grace" or "Blessings." It is a gentle and affectionate name, often used for newborn girls. In Hindu culture, the name Nanu symbolizes the divine grace and blessings of the gods bestowed upon a child.

historical_references.reference: Nanu, also known as Nanadev, was a 15th-century Maharashtrian poet and saint, who is considered an incarnation of Vishnu in the form of Narasimha. He is best known for his Marathi language devotional poetry and is regarded as a pioneer of the Marathi language literature.

Nanu or Nanak, was a Jain Tirthankara, born around the 11th or 12th century in Gujarat. He is considered the 21st Tirthankara in the present cycle of Jainism, and is believed to have attained Nirvana in Rajasthan. Nanak's teachings emphasized non-violence, compassion, and self-control.
